mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 110 D300e PHEV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement AJ20P4 (PT204) engine for the Defender 110 P400e typically costs between £2,000 and £7,500 depending on condition type: used engines from £2,000-£4,000, reconditioned from £3,500-£5,500, and rebuilt/remanufactured from £4,500-£7,500. Supply and fit adds approximately £1,000-£2,000 in labour. Dealer pricing for a full replacement can exceed £15,000-£30,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of coolant pump belt failure in a Defender 110 D300e PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0-litre Ingenium PHEV is subject to a known coolant pump drive belt issue - a safety recall (N785) was issued for 2021-2023 models. Common symptoms include overheating warnings, loss of coolant, steam from the engine bay, and in severe cases, engine shutdown and fire risk.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Defender 110 D300e PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on your vehicle's value and the extent of the damage. A typical 2021-2023 Defender 110 P400e is worth £55,000-£90,000, with newer examples exceeding £95,000. Given the high residual value of these vehicles, a rebuilt engine with warranty is almost always a sound investment. If the car is worth under £8,000 (extremely unlikely for this model), a used engine or repair may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Defender 110 D300e PHEV engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full engine replacement on a Land Rover Defender 110 P400e typically takes 3-5 working days for supply and fit through a specialist. This includes removal of the old unit, hybrid system disconnection/reconnection, preparation of the replacement engine, installation, and testing. PHEV powertrains require additional time for high-voltage system handling.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Defender 110 P400e and the D300 diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are entirely different powertrains. The P400e (often called D300e PHEV in some markets) is a 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol plug-in hybrid producing 404PS total system output. The D300 is a 3.0-litre six-cylinder diesel mild hybrid (MHEV) producing 300PS and 650Nm. They share the 110 body style but have completely different engines, fuel types and hybrid architectures.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a replacement Defender 110 D300e PHEV engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt or reconditioned engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines may come with a shorter warranty (typically 3-6 months) depending on the supplier. Always confirm exact warranty terms - including what is and isn't covered - with your chosen specialist before purchase.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 D300e PHEV - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Land Rover Defender 110 P400e (often referred to in some markets as D300e PHEV) is the plug-in hybrid variant of the L663-generation Defender, launched in September 2020 as a 110-body-only model. Positioned as the eco-conscious choice in the Defender range, the P400e combines a 2.0-litre four-cylinder Ingenium petrol engine with a 105kW electric motor and a 19.2kWh lithium-ion battery for a total system output of 404PS.

milestones.description: P400e PHEV introduced exclusively on the Defender 110 body style, pairing the 2.0-litre Ingenium petrol (AJ20P4 / PT204) with an 85kW permanent magnet synchronous motor and 13.1kWh battery
2023 - Coolant pump drive belt recall issued for Ingenium I4 2.0L PHEV engines due to risk of belt detachment, overheating and fire
P400e name replaced by P300e in some markets, retaining the same 2.0-litre Ingenium four-cylinder PHEV powertrain
present - Updated P300e PHEV continues production with refined calibration

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Defender 110 D300e PHEV is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.commonFailure: Coolant pump drive belt failure is the most widely reported issue on the 2.0-litre Ingenium PHEV engine. The coolant pump drive belt can become damaged, leading to detachment or destruction, loss of coolant flow, rapid engine overheating, and subsequent rupture of a plastic elbow in the cooling circuit. A safety recall (N785) was issued for vehicles manufactured between 2021-2023. Typical failure reported from around 30,000-50,000 miles depending on usage.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 D300e PHEV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 2.0-litre Ingenium PHEV is a sophisticated but complex powertrain. The most significant reliability concern centres on the coolant pump drive belt - a known failure point that has prompted a JLR safety recall. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include updated components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Coolant Pump Drive Belt Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 D300e PHEV AJ20P4 Suffers Premature Belt Failure
problems.affectedModels: Land Rover Defender 110 D300e PHEV (AJ20P4 / PT204, 2021-2023 particularly)
problems.rootCause: The Ingenium I4 2.0L PHEV coolant pump drive belt can become damaged, leading to detachment or destruction. Loss of coolant flow causes the engine to rapidly overheat, rupturing a plastic elbow in the cooling circuit. Coolant can leak onto the turbocharger's heat shield, creating a risk of fire in the engine compartment.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant pump drive belt and inspect cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: Best for vehicles approaching 30,000-40,000 miles with no symptoms yet - prevents catastrophic failure
Best if engine has overheated and sustained internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2021-2023 Land Rover Defender 110 P400e is worth approximately £55,000-£90,000, with newer examples exceeding £95,000. For a Defender 110 PHEV valued under ~£8,000 (unlikely for this model), a used engine or repair may make more sense than a full rebuilt unit. For all realistic values of this premium vehicle (£55,000+), a rebuilt engine with warranty is almost always justified - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If your Defender 110 P400e has not yet experienced coolant pump belt failure but is approaching 30,000-40,000 miles, preventative belt replacement at a specialist is strongly recommended - it is far cheaper than a full engine replacement later. If the belt has already failed and the engine has overheated, replacement with a rebuilt engine (with updated cooling system components) is usually the most cost-effective long-term solution, particularly given the high residual value of these vehicles.

problems.recommendation: If you experience engine misfires or rough running in your Defender 110 P400e, have the CVVL system diagnosed promptly.
